name: Apprentice's Wand
lore: A plain rod of ash, handed to every apprentice on the day of their first spell. It does one thing, and does it faithfully. Masters keep theirs long after they have outgrown it.
text: A single bolt, as you were taught

name: Twin-Headed Staff
lore: Carved for twin sisters who studied under one master and would not share. When one fell in the catacombs, the other went on casting through both heads, and never cast alone again.
text: Two bolts side by side, each a little weaker

name: Drowned Orb
lore: A glass sphere from the floor of the flooded crypts, still full of the water that drowned them. Spells cast through it behave like water in a stone basin: they strike the walls and roll back into the room.
text: Your bolts bounce off walls twice

name: Shepherd's Crook
lore: A shepherd who took holy orders kept his crook and blessed it, so that nothing sent out with it would be lost. Bolts cast with it wander out and come home, like a flock at dusk.
text: Your bolts come back to you, striking twice

name: Mourner's Censer
lore: Swung at funerals to carry prayers upward in three plumes of smoke. The prayers never climbed far, but they spread wide, and so does the magic that smoulders in it now.
text: Three bolts fan out, but fall short

name: Gravewarden's Spear
lore: The wardens at the ossuary's gates were given one spear each, and one order: nothing passes. Magic cast through it is slow and heavy, and it stops for nothing in its way.
text: One slow, heavy bolt that passes through every foe

name: Serpent Rod
lore: A rod of green bronze shaped like a coiling adder, taken from a heretic's grave. Its bolts slither from side to side and are hard to see coming, as its owner once was.
text: Your bolts weave like a serpent

name: Ember Sigil
lore: A brass seal, still warm from the chapel's last fire. It once sealed letters meant to be burned after reading. Worn close to the heart, it lends its heat to every spell.
text: Your bolts burn hotter

name: Pilgrim's Boots
lore: Worn thin by a pilgrim who walked every road to the old chapel and never once stumbled. The leather remembers each step, and will not let its wearer fall, not even into the pits below.
text: Swift feet that do not fear the drop

name: Rosary of Haste
lore: Its beads were worn smooth by a priest who prayed faster than anyone in the order, to reach the last bead before the candle burned down. Some of that hurry stayed in the beads.
text: Your prayers, and your bolts, come quicker

name: Bone Lens
lore: A disc of bone, polished thin enough to see light through, ground from the relic of a seer. Look through it, and a bolt sees past the first thing in its way.
text: Your bolts pierce the first foe they strike

name: Reliquary Shard
lore: A shard of the chapel's great reliquary, which once held the heart of a saint no one remembers. The heart is gone, but the shard still beats faintly, and lends its strength to yours.
text: One more heart, and every heart made whole

name: Saint's Knucklebone
lore: Sold a hundred times to a hundred pilgrims, and yet this one is real. Where it passes, the dead do not rest quietly: they burst apart in holy fire.
text: The dead burst into bolts

name: Mourning Bell
lore: A handbell rung at the head of funeral processions. It still rings on its own when blood is spilled nearby, and what it rings for, it answers.
text: When you are struck, the bell answers

name: Mason's Chisel
lore: The chisel that carved the ossuary's niches, left by the mason who carved the last one and climbed into it. Stone remembers the chisel, and gives way to it.
text: Your bolts crack stone

name: Raven's Eye
lore: Ravens were kept in the chapel yard to watch for grave robbers. This eye, set in silver, still watches, and now and then it finds the weak spot in whatever you strike.
text: One bolt in five strikes thrice as hard

name: Cracked Mirror
lore: A scrying mirror that cracked when its owner saw their own death in it. Every image in it is split in two, and every spell that strikes true breaks in half and flies on.
text: Your bolts split in two when they strike

name: Hawk-Bone Fletching
lore: Feathers and hollow bones from a hunting hawk, once bound to arrows that never missed. Bound to a spell instead, they lend it the hawk's speed and reach.
text: Your bolts fly faster and farther

name: Ram's Skull
lore: The skull of the ram that led the chapel's flock, its horns worn smooth by a lifetime of shoving. Its stubbornness outlived it, and passes into every bolt you cast.
text: Your bolts hurl foes back

name: Leech Jar
lore: A barber-surgeon's jar, stoppered with wax. The leeches inside died long ago, but their hunger did not, and now and then it shares what it takes from your foes.
text: Every tenth foe put to rest gives back half a heart

name: Candle Moth
lore: A pale moth that followed a lantern into the crypts and never found its way out. It has taken to your light instead, and stings anything that comes too close to it.
text: A pale moth flutters about you, stinging your foes

name: Rune of Fen-Nex
lore: A disc of indigo stone with a fox's face cut in it, its runes still lit. Whoever carries it down is followed by Fen-Nex, a small fox of rune-light that bites at their foes, and grows the deeper the way goes, until it is what it was before it was bound.
text: Fen-Nex follows at your heel and bites your foes; it grows with every floor

name: Weeping Skull
lore: The skull of a penitent who wept every day of their life for a sin no one ever learned. It weeps still, and circles its keeper, swallowing what would harm them.
text: A weeping skull circles you, swallowing shots

name: Unbroken Oath
lore: A knight's oath, written on vellum and sealed in lead: to leave every battle without a wound. Keep the oath, and now and then it keeps you.
text: Win a fight unhurt, and half a heart returns

name: Sexton's Keyring
lore: The sexton kept the keys to every door, gate and crypt of the Wardens' chapel, and to some of the doors below. Warded locks still remember the sexton's hand, and step aside.
text: Three bone keys, and a vault's ward yields to you once a floor

name: Miser's Purse
lore: Found clutched in the hand of a man buried with his fortune. The coins are long gone, but the purse still swells with pride as it fills, and lends that weight to your spells.
text: Your bolts strike harder for every ten obols you hoard

name: Glyphwright's Chalk
lore: Chalk ground from the bones of the blast-scribes, the mages who cleared the catacombs for the first diggers. It holds five glyphs of their craft, and draws each one wider.
text: Five blast glyphs, and your blasts reach half again as far

name: Ferryman's Obol
lore: The coin the Ferryman hands back when he turns a soul away from the river. Carry it, and he keeps paying you: an obol for every fight that did not send you to him.
text: Every fight you win, the ferryman pays you an obol

name: Warding Band
lore: A ring of pale iron worn by the blast-scribes, who learned the hard way that a glyph does not care who chalked it. The band cares, and turns the blast aside.
text: Your glyphs spare you, and their fuse burns faster

name: Grave Lantern
lore: Carried by the sexton on his night rounds. It burns with the pale light that seeps through cracks from rooms the living have walled up, and shows the hidden places.
text: Cracked walls glow for you, and the hidden cell shows on your map

name: Pedlar's Scale
lore: A bent brass scale from a pedlar who traded with the dead and never once cheated them. The shades remember honest dealing, and ask less of whoever carries it.
text: The shade weighs your obols kindly: his prices fall by 30%

name: Mask of the Drowned
lore: Pressed from the face of a sister who drowned in the flooded crypts, it kept her last breath. Every spell takes on that breath's fury, but dark water closes in around your eyes.
text: Your bolts strike twice as hard, but the dark closes in

curse.cleansed: Your bolts strike half again as hard

name: Chain of the Penitent
lore: Penitents wore these chains down to the crypts to pray. Pain slides off its wearer for a while after each blow, as penance should, but the weight never lets them hurry.
text: Wounds spare you longer, but the chain drags

curse.cleansed: Wounds spare you a little longer

name: Leaden Heart
lore: A heart of cast lead, left on a tomb by someone who could not bear to love again. It gives you more heart than you had, but it is heavy, and your bolts sink before they fly far.
text: Two more hearts, but your bolts fall short

name: Bloodied Covenant
lore: A pact signed in blood with something that lives beneath the ossuary. It lends your spells real strength, and before every fight it takes its due: a little of the blood that signed it.
text: Your bolts strike harder, but every fight takes a tithe of blood

name: Emberwood Wand
lore: Cut from a beam of the old pyre-house after the fire that took it, and it never quite went out. Hold it close and it is warm; point it at something and the warmth leaves in a hurry.
text: Your bolts set foes burning, but fly a little shorter

name: Tome of Whispers
lore: A book that was never written, only overheard. Read from it aloud and your bolts go slowly and softly, and they listen for the nearest heartbeat, and they find it.
text: Slow bolts that curve towards foes, and strike harder

name: Mana Lantern
lore: The sextons carried these to find their way through the lower crypts. It burns no oil. It burns whatever the one who carries it has left to give, and it gives back a little more.
text: You can hold more mana

name: Candle of the Vigil
lore: Lit for the dead in the chapel above and carried down when no one was left to tend it. Every time the fighting stops, its flame stands straight again, and so does something in you.
text: Every fight you win refills some mana

name: Frostbitten Ring
lore: Taken from a pilgrim found frozen upright in a crypt that was never cold. The ring is colder than the finger ever was, and now and then the cold slips out with a bolt.
text: Every fifth cast of your bolts chills what it strikes

name: Stormglass Pendant
lore: Glass from a window of the chapel, struck by lightning and never cooled. Something in it still flickers, and it wants to finish what the storm began in anything the storm has touched.
text: Shocked foes take more damage from your bolts

name: Thurible of Ash
lore: The sextons swung it over the pyres to carry the smoke up and away. It still remembers the rite: whatever falls burning, it gathers up, and scatters the embers over the next in line.
text: Foes that die burning set their neighbours burning

name: Witch's Knot
lore: A cord knotted nine times by someone who knew how close a spell sits to a last breath. The nearer you come to dying, the tighter it pulls, and the less your magic asks of you.
text: Your spells cost less at half health or below

name: Crown of Thorns
lore: Worn by a penitent who believed pain was the only honest price for power. The thorns go deep. Every spell you cast comes out sharper for it, and your heart never quite closes around them.
text: Your spells strike far harder, but you lose a heart

name: Hungering Tome
lore: Its pages drink. Feed it the dead and it spills their last warmth back into you as magic; stop feeding it, and your own magic runs dry, because the tome is not willing to share its meal.
text: Every foe you put to rest refills mana, but mana no longer comes back on its own

curse.cleansed: Every foe you put to rest refills a little mana

name: Pilgrim's Cowl
lore: Wool gone dark with crypt damp, the hood of a pilgrim who came down to pray and never climbed back up. It keeps the cold of the crypts off your thoughts, and keeps the thoughts in.
text: You can hold a little more mana, and wounds spare you a moment longer

name: Pendulum of Hours
lore: The weight from the sextons' clock, which kept the hours of the dead long after the living stopped listening. Its bolts swing out and back as it did, first one way and then the other, and strike all the harder for the swing.
text: Your bolts swing out in a curve, left on one cast and right on the next, and strike harder

name: Lodestar Wand
lore: A wand tipped with a sliver of lodestone that pulls at its own bolts. They fly as far as it lets them, then stop and hang in the air like stars, waiting for something to walk into them.
text: Your bolts stop where their range ends and hang there as small stars that strike what touches them

name: Twin Vigil Candles
lore: Two candles from a vigil kept over twins, lit side by side and never let go out. They burn brightest for whoever stays still beside them, as the mourners did, and lend that stillness a steadier hand.
text: Standing still, your bolts strike half again as hard; two candle flames at your shoulders show it

name: Ossuary Choir
lore: A little bone flute carved from a chorister's finger. The dead of the ossuary still know their parts: put enough of them to rest in one place and they take up the old hymn, and the living in that room do not enjoy it.
text: Every fifth foe you put to rest in a room makes the choir sing: every foe in the room is struck

name: Echo Stone
lore: A pebble from the deepest cistern, where every sound comes back twice. Throw a word at a wall down there and it returns; throw a bolt, and the stone makes sure it does too.
text: A bolt that strikes a wall echoes back the way it came, once

name: Blood Moon Pendant
lore: A disc of red glass that the grave-robbers wore on the nights they worked. It does nothing for the careful. For the hurt and the desperate it quickens the hand and reddens everything it throws.
text: At half health or less, your bolts fly faster and come quicker, in crimson

name: Salt Circle
lore: A pouch of grave salt, the kind the sextons poured round a fresh grave so the dead would keep to it. Stand still long enough and it spills of its own accord into a ring the walking dead will not cross.
text: Stand still for a moment and a ring of salt forms round you that walking foes can't cross

name: Gilded Halo
lore: Taken from a reliquary's saint, whose bones did not need it any more. It marks whatever you strike first as the saint once marked the unworthy, and the mark stays until the thing falls.
text: The first bolt to strike each foe sanctifies it: it takes more from everything, and nothing heals it

name: Ferryman's Lantern
lore: The lamp that hangs from the Ferryman's prow, by which the drifting souls find the crossing. Carried through the crypts, it draws them to you instead, and loosens whatever the hexed still owe.
text: Hexed foes give back half again the mana, and soul motes come twice as often

name: Hart's Antler
lore: A tine broken from the antlers of the white hart that walks the reliquary. Something of its light is still in the bone, and now and then it comes out of your bolts as a lance.
text: Every sixth cast is a lance of light that pierces and sanctifies

name: Gravemonger's Contract
lore: A contract with a gravemonger, one who bought what the dead had on them. It pays well for every body, and in return it takes the living's share: no mending for the one who signs it, and everything dearer.
text: Half the foes you put to rest leave an obol, but fights won leave no hearts and hearts cost twice as much

curse.cleansed: Now and then a foe you put to rest leaves an obol

name: The Last Rite
lore: The words the abbesses said over the dying, written on a strip of linen. Read over you in advance, they hold death off once for every floor you go down, and take a little of your heart to do it.
text: Once a floor, a killing blow is refused and you rise with half a heart, but you lose a heart

curse.cleansed: Once every two floors, a killing blow is refused
